questions.q: What are the first two steps to creating an Azure Blob Storage linked service?
options: Manage hub → Linked services → New, then search for and select the Blob Storage connector
Author hub → Pipelines → New, then write JSON by hand
Monitor hub → Refresh, then select Blob Storage from a dropdown
Home page → Ingest, then skip straight to building a pipeline
questions.explain: Every linked service, regardless of connector, starts the same way: Manage → Linked services → New, then finding the specific connector in the gallery.

questions.q: Which authentication method requires no stored credential at all?
options: Managed identity (system- or user-assigned)
Account key
Anonymous authentication
Shared access signature
questions.explain: A managed identity is an Azure-managed identity — there's no secret sitting in the linked service that could leak, expire, or need rotating.

questions.q: Why is Account key authentication generally avoided beyond a learning environment?
options: The key grants full access to the entire storage account, not just a scoped portion
It's the slowest authentication method available
It only works with public, unauthenticated containers
Azure Blob Storage doesn't actually support it
questions.explain: An account key is a broad credential — anyone with it has full access to the whole storage account, which is riskier than a scoped SAS token or an identity-based method.

questions.q: What does Test connection actually catch, before you've built anything further?
options: Problems like a typo in the storage account name or a blocking firewall rule
Nothing — it's a purely cosmetic button
Only syntax errors in DAX formulas
Whether the pipeline has been published yet
questions.explain: Testing the connection catches connectivity problems immediately, before you've built a dataset or pipeline on top of a linked service that was never going to work.

questions.q: Which authentication method is scoped and time-limited, rather than granting full account access?
options: Shared access signature (SAS)
Account key
Anonymous authentication
None of the six methods are scoped
questions.explain: A SAS token grants narrower, time-limited access — safer than a full account key, though still a credential that has to be managed and eventually renewed.
